apps/console/src/pages/review/compare.test.tsx::rules > an unjudged B fixes nothing: unmeasured is not a pass
apps/console/src/pages/review/compare.test.tsx::rules > a rule A failed that B did not check is not fixed
apps/console/src/pages/review/compare.test.tsx::gate checks > lists only the checks that flipped, in tone, and counts the rest

apps/console/src/pages/review/compare.test.tsx::quality > lists the dimension that moved most first, with both rates

apps/console/src/pages/review/compare.test.tsx::the compare route > prints flipped checks, the figures and the mix

deviations_from_card: (1) The view is CompareView.tsx, not Compare.tsx: Compare.tsx and compare.ts resolve to the same module on a case-insensitive disk (Windows), which rendered `undefined`; compare.ts keeps the card's name. (2) Judge.tsx and names.ts untouched: dimRows is already exported and compare.ts reuses it and the names as they are. (3) 'Compare with previous' is a tab in the session tab bar (role=tab, navigates like the others) rather than an <a>, because ui/Tabs is button-based and wrapping it would break its sticky position; it targets review/<previous>/compare/<this> so A=before, B=after. (4) index.ts: to keep the entry under its 286,000 line (9 B headroom at HEAD) the breadcrumb table now names only the tabs that do not humanize to themselves (types, calls); Timeline/Player/Judge/Moderation/Compare come from the shell's humanize fallback, same text. (5) Tests and implementation are one commit (the tests cannot compile without compare.ts), plus a separate budget commit taken under the lock.
